review_reference: Owner request of 2026-11-02 in chat (D-Eminence): "i need the access pin and emergency to work in demo account now and fill both patient and ehr with the informaton you filled in the demo video"
evidence: 0102 (sealed demo story), owner request of 2026-11-02 by D-Eminence in chat: "i need the access pin and emergency to work in demo account now and fill both patient and ehr with the informaton you filled in the demo video"; unsigned until the owner signs. Backward compatible: no table, column, index, constraint, policy, trigger or existing function changes; pg_dump --schema-only of a 0101 database before and after differs only by three new functions in schema identity and their comments, all owned by the applier and granted to no role (revoked from PUBLIC in the file and in runtime-grants.sql, whose only change is that revoke). No service calls them, so every image now running gives the same answers. WHAT IT DOES. identity.demo_story_install(pin_hash) (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp) fills the 0098 sealed demo tenant with the demo video's made-up story; identity.demo_story_context and identity.demo_story_lab_result are its helpers. It runs on Amazon RDS only (rds_superuser exists), as 0098's install does; everywhere else (CI, acceptance, rehearsals) nothing is seeded and the suite sealed-demo-story calls the seed with its own test hash. On production it: renames the ten demo patients (Adaeze Okafor, born 1991-03-04; Chinedu Okafor; Abubakar Bello, Halima Yusuf, Emeka Nwosu, Ngozi Eze, Musa Ibrahim, Funke Adebayo, Ifeanyi Okeke, Zainab Lawal; Health IDs unchanged), the two patient logins' display names, and the staff login's display name and staff name (Dr Tunde Bello), each only from 0098's own value; adds the hospital, HMO and health information the patient portal counts, where the patient saved none; stores the owner's PIN hash ($2a$12$, pgcrypto, the PIN in no file) as identity.set_my_patient_access_pin stores a PIN, for Patient One and Two where they have no PIN row, revoking no grant; writes, as the demo login's doctor membership at Demo Hospital through 0098's shares, Adaeze's completed visit six weeks before the apply and today's visit in progress (vitals, signed notes, diagnoses Z88.0, D50.9, B54, ferrous sulphate, artemether-lumefantrine, paracetamol, a malaria rapid test and a full blood count) and Chinedu checked in today; sends the six orders with ehr.send_order_route and accepts them with lab.accept_order_route and pharmacy.accept_order_route at Demo Laboratory and Demo Pharmacy; writes the Lab's steps to two entered results (not checked or released: lab.validate_result_governance needs a second person, and the demo has one login) and two dispensings (6 and 18 tablets), which complete those two routes; adds two Outreach campaigns and four registrations, not linked to the campaign (outreach.validate_registration_campaign_write, 0045, reads the campaign member FOR SHARE, which forced row-level security refuses an owner without BYPASSRLS because outreach.campaign_members has no UPDATE policy; the same check runs for outreach-api, so a live registration into a campaign may meet the same refusal: reported, not changed). Every row is demo (55000 SEALED_DEMO_STORY_NOT_DEMO otherwise). Refusals, each 55000 with nothing written: SEALED_DEMO_STORY_LOGINS_NOT_READY (the three demo logins not all active), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ORDERS_OFF (cross_facility_orders_enabled or cross_facility_route_access_enabled off), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_SHARE_MISSING (a 0098 share at Demo Hospital revoked), and, asked before any order command runs so the release never stops inside one, SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ROLE_MISSING (a demo membership inactive or a send or receive permission gone), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_DESTINATION_OFF (Demo Laboratory or Demo Pharmacy not eligible to receive, for example unlisted by support), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_PATIENT_RESTRICTED (Adaeze or Chinedu not active, without a Health ID, or with a deny directive naming a destination) and SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ORDER_LIMIT (the daily send, pair, open-order or wrong-patient limits); the Health IDs and attestation texts given to the commands are read from the database; 22023 SEALED_DEMO_STORY_PIN_HASH_INVALID for any hash but bcrypt cost 12. Once only: a second call changes nothing. Nothing is sent: the order notices (sent, accepted) are marked read in the same transaction, so no web push is due; no lab or pharmacy outbox row for results or dispensings, no identity outbox row, no delivery attempt; the accept commands queue LabWorkItemCreated and PharmacyWorkItemCreated integration events as for any order, which no notification workflow reads. Audit: one row of the migration's own per row written (actor system, provenance migration, source system hid-sealed-demo, correlation id 0102-sealed-demo-story, ids only, the PIN's with its cost and never the hash; 56 rows) and one story row with counts; no audit row names a patient or clinician; the order commands add their own 14 system rows. Preconditions (catalog reads, 55000/42501, nothing applied): 0001-0101 objects present, none of 0102's, 40 relied-on function bodies byte for byte (md5 of prosrc), the two profile tables' owner policies naming the applier, CREATE on schema identity. Locks: none up front; on production the seed takes ROW EXCLUSIVE on the tables it writes and row locks on ten patients, three accounts and one staff record until commit. Measured on throwaway PostgreSQL 16: apply 13 ms (functions only); the forced seed in one transaction about 1.1 s, also run whole as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (every schema, table and function reowned, the 0094 owner policies naming it), so every write passed the tables' forced row-level security, triggers and the 0098 seal guards, with the same 56 audit rows. Proven on throwaway PostgreSQL 16: fresh install 0001-0102 (103 files) and upgrade from 0101 (plan 1 pending, dry run rolls back, apply, then 0 pending; the file again answers 0102: already applied), roles bootstrapped and verified, every DB suite green on both, the new suite sealed-demo-story green (refusals, the owner's hash stored verbatim at cost 12 and accepted by pgcrypto without any PIN tried, the seed, row-level security reads by the EHR, Lab, Pharmacy and Outreach runtimes, nothing sent, the audit, idempotency, the PIN at Demo Hospital with the suite's own test PIN, break-glass on Abubakar Bello and Adaeze), the migration ledger, release contract and release-gate tests. Before signing, the owner runs the read-only query in the file's header on production: rds 1, active_logins 3, orders_on true, roles_ok true, hospital_shares 2, destinations_on true, patients_open true, limits_ok true, pins 0, story 0; any other answer is the matching named refusal, and the release would stop with nothing applied. Proven on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with the role rds_superuser present (so 0098 and 0102 seed as on production): with Demo Laboratory unlisted the header query answered destinations_on false and the dry run and apply both stopped with 0102: SEALED_DEMO_STORY_DESTINATION_OFF and nothing applied; with every answer as required the dry run rolled back and the apply seeded the story with the owner's hash (pins 2, orders 6, 56 audit rows), then 0 pending.
